name: Byron Bay
tagline: Surf, lighthouse walks and a laid-back beach town
summary: Byron Bay is a relaxed surf town on Australia's most easterly point. Walk the Cape Byron track to the lighthouse to spot dolphins and migrating whales, surf the Pass, swim at Wategos, explore hinterland villages and rainforest waterfalls, and eat well in a town known for its cafés.
seasonNote: Whales June to November; summer holidays are crowded and pricey.
arrival: Fly to Ballina or Gold Coast airport (35 to 50 minutes away).
gettingAround: Walk and bike in town; a car for the hinterland.
foodTip: Brunch cafés, fish and chips, acai bowls.

name: Airlie Beach (Whitsundays)
tagline: Gateway to Whitehaven Beach and the reef
summary: Airlie Beach is the lively launch point for the Whitsunday Islands. Sail to the pure white silica sand of Whitehaven Beach and the swirling Hill Inlet lookout, snorkel the Great Barrier Reef, fly over Heart Reef, and swim in the town's lagoon pool while stinger season keeps you out of the sea.
seasonNote: Dry winter June to October; stinger season November to May (wear a stinger suit).
arrival: Fly to Proserpine (35 minutes away) or Hamilton Island.
gettingAround: Walk in town; boats to the islands.
buyTip: Not much; it's about the water.

name: Apollo Bay (Great Ocean Road)
tagline: The Twelve Apostles and the Great Ocean Road
summary: Apollo Bay is a fishing town halfway along the Great Ocean Road, one of the world's great coastal drives. Drive the cliff road from Lorne, spot koalas at Kennett River, walk through Otway rainforest to waterfalls, see Cape Otway lighthouse and watch sunset over the Twelve Apostles limestone stacks and Loch Ard Gorge.
seasonNote: Summer and early autumn are warmest; winter is wild and quiet.
arrival: About 3 hours by car from Melbourne along the coast.
foodTip: Fish and chips, local crayfish and Otway produce.

name: Kangaroo Island
summary: Kangaroo Island is a large, wild island off South Australia, full of animals. See sea lions on the beach at Seal Bay, kangaroos and koalas in the bush, the wind-sculpted Remarkable Rocks and Admirals Arch with its fur seals, and taste local honey, gin and oysters.
seasonNote: Spring to autumn; winter is cool and windy.
arrival: Ferry from Cape Jervis (45 minutes; 2 hours' drive from Adelaide) or a 30-minute flight.
gettingAround: A car is essential; distances are big.
foodTip: Oysters, marron, Ligurian bee honey and local gin.

connections.note: Drive to Cape Jervis, then the SeaLink ferry.

name: Broome
tagline: Camels at sunset on Cable Beach
summary: Broome is a pearling town on the edge of the Kimberley with turquoise water and red cliffs. Ride camels along Cable Beach at sunset, see the Staircase to the Moon on the tidal flats, find dinosaur footprints at Gantheaume Point, watch films at the world's oldest outdoor cinema and learn the pearling history of Chinatown.
seasonNote: Dry season May to October; the wet season is hot, humid and stormy.
gettingAround: Hire car or the town bus.
foodTip: Barramundi, mud crab and Asian-influenced pearling food.

name: Bay of Islands
tagline: Islands, dolphins and the birthplace of New Zealand
summary: The Bay of Islands is a subtropical bay of 144 islands in Northland. Visit the Waitangi Treaty Grounds where New Zealand's founding treaty was signed, sail to the Hole in the Rock, swim with or watch dolphins, explore historic Russell, and drive north to Cape Reinga where the Tasman Sea meets the Pacific.
seasonNote: Summer is best for sailing and swimming.
arrival: About 3.5 hours by car from Auckland, or fly to Kerikeri.
gettingAround: A car; ferries between Paihia and Russell.
foodTip: Fish and chips, Kerikeri citrus and local oysters.

name: Franz Josef and Fox Glaciers
summary: Franz Josef and Fox are two glaciers on New Zealand's wild West Coast, falling from the Southern Alps almost to the rainforest. Take a heli-hike onto the ice, walk the valley trails to glacier viewpoints, soak in rainforest hot pools, and catch the mirror reflections of Aoraki/Mount Cook in Lake Matheson at dawn.
seasonNote: Weather changes fast year round; keep a spare day for flights.
arrival: About 5 hours by car from Queenstown or 2 hours from Hokitika.

name: Kaikōura
summary: Kaikōura is a small seaside town where snow-capped mountains rise straight from the ocean. A deep sea canyon close to shore brings sperm whales, dolphins, albatross and fur seals year round. Take a whale-watching boat or flight, walk the peninsula past seal colonies and eat fresh crayfish, the dish the town is named for.
seasonNote: Whales year round; summer is calmest for boats.
arrival: About 2.5 hours by car from Christchurch, or the scenic Coastal Pacific train.

name: Port Vila
tagline: Blue holes, lagoons and a live volcano
summary: Port Vila is the easygoing capital of Vanuatu, on Efate island. Swim in the Blue Lagoon and Mele Cascades, see kastom villages, snorkel at Hideaway Island's underwater post office, eat at the Mamas' market, and fly to Tanna island to stand at the rim of Mount Yasur, one of the world's most accessible active volcanoes.
seasonNote: Dry season May to October; cyclone season November to April.
arrival: Flights from Brisbane, Sydney, Auckland and Fiji.
gettingAround: Minibuses (B on the plate) flagged anywhere; a rental for the island loop.
foodTip: Lap lap, fresh coconut crab and Santo beef.

name: Apia (Samoa)
tagline: Ocean trenches, beach fales and fa'a Samoa
summary: Apia is Samoa's small capital on Upolu island. Climb down into the To Sua Ocean Trench to swim, sleep in an open beach fale at Lalomanu, slide down Papaseea rocks, visit Robert Louis Stevenson's mansion, and take the ferry to Savai'i for lava fields and blowholes, all in a culture where tradition (fa'a Samoa) is strong.
seasonNote: Dry season May to October; cyclone season November to April.
arrival: Flights from Auckland, Brisbane, Sydney, Fiji and Honolulu.
gettingAround: Colourful local buses or a rental car; ferries to Savai'i.
foodTip: Oka (raw fish in coconut), palusami and umu feasts.
